newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 4.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
HOME MINISTER, STATE GOVERNOR CLASH SNOWBALLS

Prime minister Deve Gowda intervened after the CPI took offence to Uttar Pradesh Governor's rejoinder to home minister's statement in parliament that the state was slipping towards anarchy. Gowda summoned governor Bhandari to Delhi and asked him to sort out the matter with the home minister. Bhandari met the minister and invited him to Uttar Pradesh to assess the situation for himself and suggest remedies.
The Pioneer
BUNGLING ON WHEAT FRONT CONTINUES

The government's efforts to normalise wheat supplies has been hit by difficulties in unloading the foodgrain at ports. The Food Minister admitted logistical problems persisted at the Indian ports where, apart from wheat, other cargo had to be handled simultaneously. Other problems include the relative inaccessibility of areas where the imported wheat was to be reached, availability of railway wagons and the Food Corporation's poor infrastructure.
The Times Of India
SECURITY, SECRECY MARK MICROSOFT CHIEF'S ARRIVAL

Unprecedented secrecy shrouded the visit of Bill Gates, the chief executive of Microsoft. Though Gates arrived in New Delhi on Monday noon, Microsoft officials handling his visit said he would arrive late March 3, 1997. He was declared as the personal guest of the Prime Minister. Gates' itinerary was also kept secret and so was the purpose of his visit, though details of the three meetings he would address were known.
The Economic Times
PETRO PRICE HIKE DELAYED AS GLOBAL CRUDE SLIDES

The government could now delay the decision on a petroleum price hike till June, following the fall in international prices of crude. The imminent hike, which was necessary to restore the financial position of the oil companies, could now be delayed till such time the oil companies exhausted their borrowing limit. The oil pool deficit, too, was expected to shrink following the fail in prices. The Petroleum Ministry, however, said the cabinet was yet to take a decision and the proposal for a price hike was being studied by the Finance Ministry.
INDIA DEPOSITARY RECEIPTS RECOMMENDED

The working group set up to redraft the Companies Act recommended introduction of buyback of shares, Indian Depositary Receipts (IDRs), and optional consolidation of group accounts. The panel recommended setting up of IDRs, similar to American Depositary Receipts or Global Depositary Receipts.
Financial Express
RUPEE SPURTS AGAINST DOLLAR

The rupee appreciated against the U.S. currency as exporters holding long-dollar positions sold heavily after the budget announcements seemed to favour stronger inflows. Most exporters expected the budget would include measures to support the dollar slightly above the 35.90 rupee level. Opening around 35.89 rupees the dollar crumbled to touch an intra- day low of 35.80 on heavy selling. It, however, found support at 35.8300-35.8350, the rate at which the central bank (RBI) intervened, dealers said.
PAYOUT TAX WILL MARGINALISE RATE CUT BENEFITS

The impact of the ten percent tax on companies that pay dividends has substantially eroded the gains expected from the reduction in tax rates and removal of surcharge in the 1997/98 (April-March) Budget. Despite rationalisation of tax rates, companies paying the minimum alternate tax (MAT) would end up paying tax at an effective rate of above 12.9 percent, unless they cut down on dividend payout or drastically improved their bottom-lines.
PROJECT COST OF PRIVATE FIRMS DIP

The total project cost of private sector companies which have made public issues in the first 11 months of 1996/97 (April-March) has declined to 51.87 billion rupees as against a figure of 121.21 billion rupees in 1995-96. The primary market, according to Prime Database, continues to languish with the number of public issues documents submitted to Securities and Exchange Board of India declining.
Business Standard
BAT SET TO PATCH UP WITH ITC, SCRAP JOINT VENTURE PLANS

British cigarette giant BAT plc and ITC, the cigarettes-to-hotels conglomerate, were preparing to end their battle for control of the company. BAT, with a 32 percent stake, is the single largest shareholder in ITC. BAT was likely to drop the proposal for a joint venture with ITC to introduce its international cigarette brands in the country, in deference to the latter's reservations. Instead, negotiations were now on to allow ITC to manufacture and market BATs international brands, including Benson & Hedges and State Express.
TARIFF ISSUE REFERRED TO REGULATORY BODY

The Delhi High Court referred the dispute between cellular phone operators and the department of telecommunications (DoT) over fixed-to-cellular call charges, to the recently-formed Telecom Regulatory Authority (TRAI). The court described the issue as a national urgency while directing the case to the TRAI and suggested it be reviewed expeditiously. However, a stay was not granted on the DoT decision to increase tariffs for calls made from its network to cellular phones.
The Observer
PRICE BAND OF 35-40 PCT ADVOCATED

Bombay bourse president, M.G. Damani said that in view of the excellent budget, there was no point restricting the overall price band at the current level of 25 percent. This should be relaxed at least for the current week at 35 to 40 percent. He advocated that it would encourage compliance. However, he did not feel the need to change the current daily price band of 10 percent. He expected the Bombay bourse sensitive index to touch 5,000 mark by Diwali, provided the country experiences a good monsoon.
